title: Extreme cloud collisions in nearby barred galaxies
question: Confirm the existence of extended velocity features (EVFs) in the dust lanes of nearby barred galaxies and determine their physical origin using PHANGS-ALMA and PHANGS-JWST data.

evidence.quote: in this work we use a sample of 29 galaxies from the PHANGS-ALMA dataset, listed in Table 1, all classified as barred, based on their CO(2–1) morphology, by Stuber et al. (2023) (class B and C there).

recipe.goal: Construct diagnostic PP and PV maps and visually identify dust lanes and EVFs
recipe.method: Rotate each CO(2-1) datacube so the positive half of the line of nodes aligns with the negative x-axis, convert angular scales to physical kpc, integrate over velocity and spatial dimensions to create 1 PP and 2 PV maps, visually enclose bar dust lanes with contours in glue, and visually select compact, broad-lined EVFs in the PV maps.
key_parameters: 29 barred galaxies (Class B and C in Stuber et al. 2023) and 13 unbarred test galaxies (Class A and SA)
assumptions: Distances from Anand et al. (2021) and PAs of LON and inclinations from Lang et al. (2020) or Salo et al. (2015)

recipe.goal: Estimate EVF physical radii and galactocentric distances
recipe.method: Visually define a circular region on the dust lane in PP space encompassing the EVF, centre on the brightest point, fit a 2D Gaussian to the PP map to get centre coordinates (x, y) and standard deviations (sigma_x, sigma_y), and compute R_EVF and R_cen.
key_parameters: eta = sqrt(2 ln 2) = 1.18 in R_EVF = eta * sqrt(sigma_x * sigma_y)
assumptions: Surface brightness modelled as a 2D Gaussian; R_EVF is an upper limit for unresolved EVFs

recipe.goal: Measure EVF velocity dispersion and velocity spread (FWHM)
recipe.method: Extract the total integrated CO spectrum within R_EVF and fit a 1D Gaussian (single Gaussian for external galaxies, double Gaussian for Milky Way EVFs to account for overlapping components).
key_parameters: Delta v = (2 sqrt(2 ln 2)) sigma_v; MW longitude ranges l = 2.7-3.4 deg (for l=3.2 deg EVF) and l = 5.0-5.6 deg (for l=5.4 deg EVF), latitude unrestricted

recipe.goal: Calculate EVF molecular masses, virial masses, and virial parameters
recipe.method: Integrate CO intensity I_CO within R_EVF, multiply by constant alpha_CO to get M_CO, and compute M_vir = 5 sigma_v^2 R_EVF / G and alpha_vir = 2 M_vir / M_CO.
key_parameters: alpha_CO = 6.69 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1; CO(2-1)/CO(1-0) ratio = 0.70; Galactic alpha_CO(1-0) = 4.35 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1
assumptions: Constant Galactic conversion factor alpha_CO = 6.69 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1; isotropic velocity distribution and spherical uniform density for virial mass

recipe.goal: Inspect JWST 7.7 um images for low-density gas streams and substructure
recipe.method: Overlay CO(2-1) PP contours on JWST/MIRI F770W (7.7 um) images and visually inspect the bar region and EVF vicinities for resolved clumps and faint gas streams connecting to the EVFs.
assumptions: 7.7 um PAH emission traces molecular gas column density away from star-forming regions

answer_key.quantity: Fraction of barred galaxies containing EVFs

evidence.quote: We study a sample of 29 barred galaxies and find that 34% contain one or more EVFs, while the remaining lack obvious signs of EVFs.
After examining the PP and PV diagrams of the 29 galaxies in our sample, we identified EVFs in 10 out of 29 galaxies, which represents approximately 34% of the total.

answer_key.quantity: Total number of EVFs identified in barred galaxy sample

evidence.quote: In total, we identified 18 EVFs within 10 galaxies.

answer_key.quantity: Number of EVFs associated with faint 7.7 um gas streams

evidence.quote: Upon examining the 7.7 µm band observations of all galaxies with EVFs, we find that out of 18 EVF regions, 9 are associated with faint streams extending from the opposite end of the bar toward the EVF location.

answer_key.quantity: Milky Way EVF (l = 3.2 deg) velocity spread (FWHM)

evidence.quote: This yields a FWHM 70.64 ± 2.07 km s−1 for the EVF component

evidence.quote: To produce nevertheless an estimate of ∆v, we again fit a double Gaussian and consider the broadest peak to be the EVF, resulting in ∆v = 68.40 ± 4.19 km s−1.

score_reason: All underlying ALMA and JWST high-level datacubes and images are publicly available via CANFAR and MAST, and the mathematical equations for radii, masses, and virial parameters are explicitly given. However, the dust lane masks and initial circular EVF apertures were drawn manually in glue without publishing the exact region coordinates or aperture sizes, though the diagnostic plots and R_cen values allow approximate localization.
rediscovery_reason: The PHANGS-ALMA cubes are publicly available, the 18 EVFs are visually marked in the paper's figures with galactocentric radii and physical properties tabulated in Table 2, and the Gaussian fitting and virial equations are straightforward to re-implement.
